Subject: Private Plan listing & co-sell structure — BlueBridge / Redwood

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the product looked good and the team is excited to move to a private offer listing on Azure Marketplace. Microsoft has asked us to clarify whether BlueBridge will act as a reseller on the listing or if we will pursue a co-sell arrangement where Redwood remains the primary seller and BlueBridge receives a commercial split.

Can you confirm:
- What commercial splits Redwood is open to for a Marketplace private plan (percentage split, timing of payouts)?
- How billing will flow (Marketplace invoicing vs vendor invoicing to partner)?
- Any specific contract addenda or reseller language Microsoft requires for private plan listings?

I've attached our procurement form and a short list of procurement timelines. We'd like to get to an agreed form before the marketplace onboarding call with Microsoft next week (they assigned us an onboarding slot on 5/28).

Thanks,

Hi Peter — great to hear and glad the demo resonated. Looping in Ben (Sales Ops) and Marissa (Enterprise) to confirm commercial and onboarding details.

High level answers to your questions:
- Commercial split: for co-sell/private plan marketplace listings we typically work off a 70/30 revenue split (Redwood/partner) as a starting point for negotiated deals; for strategic partners we can move to 65/35 with an approved deal id and committed ARR.
- Billing flow: the typical Azure private plan flow is that Microsoft invoices the customer and remits payment to the seller account (Redwood). We then record partner splits and issue partner payouts monthly via our partner settlement process (we can invoice a partner or issue a payout depending on partner preference).
- Contract language: Microsoft requires a Marketplace Private Offer addendum and a reseller/co-sell acknowledgement. We'll need to sign the Marketplace addendum and a partner reseller addendum if BlueBridge will be shown as a reseller on the listing.

Ben — can you confirm whether our finance team prefers Redwood to remit to partner vs issuing invoices in this scenario? Also, Marissa, any marketplace ops pitfalls to watch for on the listing visibility and co-sell attribution?

Next steps: I'll schedule a triage call for early next week (Mon/Tue) and share the proposed revenue split and draft addendum once Ben confirms the payout flow.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Priya / Marissa — quick legal / ops note to confirm what we'll provide and what we need from BlueBridge: 

- Partner visibility: Microsoft allows a "co-seller" display but it depends on the partner's marketplace onboarding status; BlueBridge will need an active Partner Center ID and we will request co-sell attribution in the listing metadata. We'll coordinate with Microsoft Ops during onboarding.

- Entitlements / billing portal: Redwood will provide partner-level settlement reports (CSV) and a partner payout file. We do not currently provision a partner login into our billing console for PCI/HIPAA reasons. If BlueBridge requires direct invoice access, we can arrange an automated reporting feed (SFTP or shared Drive) for invoices and entitlements.

- Commercial split: Ops/legal prefer establishing a deal-specific split: 70/30 by default; we can approve 65/35 for committed, signed deals > $200k ARR with finance sign-off. For procurement comfort, propose: 70/30 for first-year bookings, 65/35 on renewals with annualized ACV > $200k. We avoid 60/40 unless there is a marketing/co-sell commit from BlueBridge.

- Contract docs: attaching a draft Marketplace Private Offer Addendum and a short reseller addendum for BlueBridge to review. Redlines we anticipate: revenue reporting cadence, tax handling, indemnities, and PCI/HIPAA data handling (if applicable).

Attachments: RBW_Azure_PrivatePlan_TechnicalAnnex.docx, Redwood_Azure_PrivatePlan_SOW_v3.pdf

If Peter is comfortable with the reporting cadence (monthly CSV + monthly payout), we can provide a DocuSign-ready addendum by EOD Monday. Also tagging Marissa for the Microsoft onboarding slot on 5/28.
